lessons.title: References
lessons.introduction: A reference (&) creates an alias to an existing variable so a function can modify the caller's variable directly without copying it.
conceptExplanation: Normally C++ passes a COPY of a variable into a function. Adding & (e.g., void resetCounter(int &count)) passes a direct reference to the original variable, letting the function update it and saving SRAM when passing large structs.
lessons.analogy: Pass-by-value hands someone a photocopy of your notebook; pass-by-reference hands them the actual notebook.

syntaxExplanation.summary: Place & between the parameter type and parameter name.
rules: A reference must always refer to an existing variable.
Use const Type &ref when you want zero-copy reading without allowing edits.

codeExamples.title: Modifying State via Reference
codeExamples.description: Updates a counter variable directly inside a helper function.

lineByLine.explanation: Receives a direct alias to 'errors', not a copy.

lessons.realWorldApplication: Sensor drivers pass a struct by reference (readIMU(ImuData &out)) to fill X, Y, and Z axes in one call.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting & when expecting a function to modify a caller's variable
commonMistakes.fix: Without &, only the local copy changes and the caller's variable stays unchanged.

tryItYourself.title: m08_references.ino
tryItYourself.challengePrompt: Remove the & from int &value and note why errors prints 7 instead of 0.

exercises.prompt: Add the symbol that makes val a reference parameter.
exercises.explanation: & declares a reference parameter in C++.

summary: References (&) alias existing variables without copying.
Pass-by-reference lets functions modify caller variables or return multiple outputs via a struct.

lessons.title: Pointers
lessons.introduction: A pointer (*) stores the memory address of another variable — essential for understanding Arduino libraries, buffers, and hardware registers.
objectives: Check pointers against nullptr before dereferencing.
conceptExplanation: Every variable in SRAM sits at a numeric memory address. A pointer variable holds that address. While beginners should prefer references (&) when possible, reading Arduino libraries requires understanding pointers (* and ->).
lessons.analogy: A pointer is a sticky note containing a house's street address rather than the house itself.

syntaxExplanation.summary:
int *ptr = ⌖  // store address
*ptr = 42;           // modify target through pointer
rules: Initialize pointers to a valid address or nullptr.

codeExamples.title: Reading and Writing Through a Pointer
codeExamples.description: Modifies an integer through its memory address.

lineByLine.explanation: Stores the SRAM address of pwm.
Dereferences ptr to write 255 directly into pwm.

lessons.realWorldApplication: Passing byte buffers to I2C, SPI, and radio libraries (like NRF24 or LoRa) relies on pointers.

commonMistakes.mistake: Dereferencing an uninitialized or nullptr pointer
commonMistakes.fix: Always initialize pointers and check if (ptr != nullptr) before using *ptr.

tryItYourself.title: m08_pointers.ino
tryItYourself.challengePrompt: Change *ptr = 255; to *ptr = 64; and verify pwm updates.

exercises.prompt: What does the & operator do in `int *p = &x;`?
options: Gets the memory address of variable x.
exercises.explanation: Unary & returns the SRAM address of a variable.

summary: & gets an address; * dereferences a pointer.

lessons.title: Basic Classes and Objects
lessons.introduction: A class is a blueprint combining data (like a pin number) and functions (methods like on() and off()) into reusable hardware objects.
objectives: Define a simple C++ class with private data and public methods.
Instantiate multiple independent objects from one class.
conceptExplanation: You have already used Arduino objects: Serial.println() and armServo.write(90) are methods called on objects! Writing your own class — such as StatusLed — lets you create ledRed and ledGreen with zero duplicated code.
lessons.analogy: A class is the factory blueprint for a DC motor; each object (leftMotor, rightMotor) is a separate physical motor built from that blueprint.

syntaxExplanation.summary: class Name { private: ... public: Name(...); void method(); };
rules: End class definitions with a semicolon ';'.
Initialize pins in a begin() method called inside setup(), NOT inside the constructor!

codeExamples.title: StatusLed Class with Two Objects
codeExamples.description: Controls two independent LEDs using one reusable class.

lineByLine.explanation: Calls pinMode() safely inside setup() after hardware init.

lessons.realWorldApplication: Every modern Arduino library (Servo, LiquidCrystal, Adafruit_NeoPixel) is built as a C++ class.

commonMistakes.mistake: Calling pinMode() inside a global object's constructor
commonMistakes.fix: Constructors run before Arduino initializes hardware timers/pins — always put pinMode() in a begin() method called in setup().

tryItYourself.title: m08_classes.ino
tryItYourself.challengePrompt: Turn redLed.on() inside setup() and greenLed.off().
tryItYourself.expectedBehavior: Pin 9 lights up while pin 8 turns off.

exercises.prompt: Why do Arduino classes provide a `.begin()` method instead of calling `pinMode()` in the constructor?
options: Global constructors run before Arduino finishes low-level hardware initialization.
exercises.explanation: Calling hardware setup inside begin() during setup() guarantees board peripherals are ready.

summary: Classes bundle hardware pins and behavior into reusable objects.
Put hardware setup inside begin() and call it from setup().
Classes end with a trailing semicolon.

lessons.title: Header Files (.h)
lessons.introduction: Header files (.h) declare function prototypes, constants, and class interfaces so multiple sketch tabs can share them cleanly.
objectives: Use #pragma once (or include guards) to prevent duplicate definition errors.
conceptExplanation: When a robotics sketch grows beyond 150 lines, splitting pin maps and class declarations into header files (.h) in new Arduino IDE tabs keeps your project organized and easy to navigate.
lessons.analogy: A header file is a restaurant menu listing what dishes exist without printing the kitchen's full recipes.

syntaxExplanation.summary: #pragma once at the top prevents double-inclusion.
rules: Use quotes "MyHeader.h" for local project tabs and angle brackets <Servo.h> for installed libraries.

codeExamples.title: Header Interface Example
codeExamples.description: Demonstrates include guard and prototype declarations.

lineByLine.explanation: Declaration (prototype) telling the compiler the function signature before use.

lessons.realWorldApplication: All Arduino libraries ship a .h header file that you include at the top of your sketch.

commonMistakes.fix: Including the same header twice without guards causes 'redefinition' compiler errors.

tryItYourself.title: m08_headers.ino
tryItYourself.challengePrompt: Add a second prototype `void startMotors();` and define it at the bottom.
tryItYourself.expectedBehavior: Compiles cleanly and prints messages from both functions.

exercises.prompt: What is the purpose of `#pragma once` at the top of a .h file?
options: Prevents the header from being included multiple times during compilation.
exercises.explanation: #pragma once protects against duplicate declaration errors.

summary: Header files (.h) declare interfaces, constants, and classes.
Always add #pragma once or include guards.
Use "..." for local headers and <...> for libraries.

lessons.title: Source Files (.cpp)
lessons.introduction: Source files (.cpp) hold the actual implementation code behind your .h headers, compiling cleanly into modular object files.
conceptExplanation: Arduino IDE automatically inserts #include <Arduino.h> into .ino files, but NOT into .cpp files! Whenever you move helper code into a .cpp tab, add #include <Arduino.h> at the top so pinMode, HIGH, and millis() are recognized.
lessons.analogy: If the .h file is the menu, the .cpp file is the kitchen where the recipes are actually cooked.

syntaxExplanation.summary: Include Arduino.h and your matching .h file at the top of a .cpp file.
rules: Always #include <Arduino.h> in .cpp files that call Arduino functions.

codeExamples.title: Understanding Arduino.h in .cpp
codeExamples.description: Shows why explicit Arduino.h inclusion matters in multi-file sketches.

lineByLine.explanation: Provides pinMode, digitalWrite, HIGH, LOW, and delay inside .cpp files.

lessons.realWorldApplication: Every professional Arduino library pairs LibraryName.h with LibraryName.cpp.

commonMistakes.fix: Results in 'pinMode was not declared in this scope' errors.

tryItYourself.title: m08_cpp_files.ino
tryItYourself.challengePrompt: Note how #include <Arduino.h> compiles cleanly in both .ino and .cpp files.
tryItYourself.expectedBehavior: Blinks pin 13 briefly once on startup.

exercises.prompt: Why might `digitalWrite()` fail to compile inside a separate `.cpp` file in an Arduino sketch?
options: You must explicitly add `#include <Arduino.h>` at the top of `.cpp` files.
Variables cannot be used in `.cpp` files.
exercises.explanation: Arduino IDE auto-includes Arduino.h only for .ino files, not plain .cpp files.

summary: .cpp files implement the functions declared in .h files.

lessons.title: Libraries
lessons.introduction: Libraries are pre-written, community-tested collections of .h and .cpp files that handle complex hardware protocols like Servos, I2C displays, and Wi-Fi.
objectives: Include standard and installed libraries with #include <...>.
Inspect library examples and APIs without blindly copying unknown code.
conceptExplanation: You don't need to bit-bang microsecond servo pulses from scratch when <Servo.h> already exists. However, an independent programmer reads the library's documentation to know which timers or pins it uses (for example, Servo disables PWM on pins 9 & 10 on Uno R3!).
lessons.analogy: A library is a calibrated toolbox — you still decide what to build, while the precision wrenches are ready to use.

syntaxExplanation.summary: #include <LibraryName.h> at the very top of your sketch.
rules: Check board compatibility before using a library (e.g., AVR Servo vs ESP32Servo).

codeExamples.title: Using the Standard Servo Library
codeExamples.description: Includes <Servo.h> and moves a servo to 90 degrees.

lineByLine.explanation: Binds the Servo object to pin 9.
Commands the servo horn to 90 degrees.

lessons.realWorldApplication: OLED screens (Adafruit_SSD1306), DHT sensors, and Servos all rely on libraries.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using AVR <Servo.h> on ESP32 without checking compatibility
commonMistakes.fix: ESP32 uses ESP32Servo library via Library Manager.

tryItYourself.title: m08_libraries.ino
tryItYourself.expectedBehavior: Moves a servo on pin 9 to 45 degrees on startup (Uno/Mega/Nano AVR).

exercises.prompt: Include the standard Arduino Servo header.
exercises.explanation: #include loads a library header into your sketch.

summary: Use #include <Library.h> to bring in tested hardware drivers.
Always check pin/timer side effects and board compatibility.

lessons.title: Modular Code Organization
lessons.introduction: Organizing a multi-feature robot into config.h, sensors, and actuators tabs keeps your codebase maintainable as projects scale.
objectives: Design a clean multi-tab Arduino project layout.
Centralize pin assignments and calibration constants in one place.
conceptExplanation: A well-organized Arduino folder might contain: RoverMain.ino (high-level state loop), pins.h (all pin constants), motors.h/cpp, and sensors.h/cpp. When you rewire a sensor pin, you edit exactly one line in pins.h.
lessons.analogy: A tidy electronics lab where resistors, sensors, and tools each have labeled drawers instead of one tangled pile.

syntaxExplanation.summary: Keep pins/thresholds in one config header and separate sensing from motion.
rules: The main .ino filename must match its parent folder name in Arduino IDE.

codeExamples.title: Clean Sectioned Single-File Template
codeExamples.description: Shows a clean top-to-bottom organization pattern ready to split into tabs.

lineByLine.explanation: Pins and constants grouped cleanly at the top.

lessons.realWorldApplication: Competition robotics repositories organize code by subsystem so multiple students can work without overwriting each other.

commonMistakes.mistake: Renaming a .ino file differently from its enclosing folder
commonMistakes.fix: Arduino IDE requires the main .ino file to share its folder's exact name.

tryItYourself.title: m08_organization.ino
tryItYourself.challengePrompt: Add a const int DELAY_MS = 500; in the CONFIGURATION section and use it in loop().
tryItYourself.expectedBehavior: Blinks pin 13 cleanly with centralized configuration.

exercises.prompt: In Arduino IDE, what naming rule applies to a sketch's folder and main `.ino` file?
options: The main `.ino` file must have the exact same name as its enclosing folder.
The folder must always be named 'main'.
exercises.explanation: Arduino IDE requires matching folder and primary .ino filenames.

summary: Separate configuration, helpers, and main lifecycle cleanly.
Match the main .ino filename to its parent folder name.
